SMTO-WEB-0003 — The search service refused SMTO's search

GUID: 4c8a617e-54f6-4f6a-ad14-d5620e6f8d59
Slug: web-provider-http-error
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web

What happened

  • SMTO sent your web search to the search service set up for it, but the service refused it (access denied). The refusal didn't say exactly why, so no search results came back.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Capabilities, select Configure Web, and check that the Base URL of the search provider is the right address. A wrong address can point SMTO at a page that blocks it.
  2. Ask the person who runs that search server (for example your SearXNG server) whether it blocks or requires sign-in for requests from SMTO's computer, and whether its results format for other programs is turned on. The service answered with an access refusal, which is set on the service's side, not in SMTO.
  3. Back in the Web settings, select Test connection for that provider. The test sends one small search and shows whether the service now accepts it.
  4. To keep working meanwhile, choose another enabled provider as Default provider, or set Fallback search to Also when the default provider fails, then select Save. SMTO can then search through a provider that is working.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows Connected, and a new web search in a conversation returns results.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who runs the search service. Don't assume a wrong password caused this, and don't turn off secure connection checks.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The search provider answered HTTP 401 or 403 without text identifying disabled JSON output, so the access denial's cause is unknown.

What this means

  • SearXNG search receives HTTP 401 or 403 without the specific response evidence used to classify unavailable JSON output. The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.

Why this can happen

  • SearXNG search receives HTTP 401 or 403 without the specific response evidence used to classify unavailable JSON output.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the recorded status and endpoint access configuration; distinguish authentication from permission denial.

How to fix it

  • SearXNGProvider.search in src/agent_runtime/skills/web/providers.py raises provider_http_error for 401/403 responses; check the recorded status_code and the instance's access rules (reverse-proxy auth, IP allow lists, limiter/bot detection) and that search.formats in the SearXNG settings.yml includes json. Then run Test connection from the Web Skill configuration; keep TLS verification enabled.
  • Inspect the recorded HTTP status and provider health before another read.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected endpoint permits the authorized search and returns a valid results list.

What not to do

  • Do not infer a password failure from every HTTP rejection or disable TLS checks.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
